name: Every recorded session says who played it
summary: The onboarding gate's sleeping-spot bar was voided because the player had already been shown the cot in earlier sessions. That fact — the single most important thing about that session — lives only in a paragraph of prose in the roadmap. None of the recorded sessions carry who played them, whether they were fresh, or whether anyone spoke during play, so no score computed from them can be trusted on its own however well the arithmetic works.
requirements: playtests/<session>/session.json recording tester, whether they were fresh to the game, whether they were prompted, and who attests to it
The ten existing session folders backfilled from the roadmap's own prose, each marked as attested rather than measured
tools/pull_session.sh writes the record when it shelves a session, so this cannot drift again
Product's gate scorecard reads the conditions rather than assuming them
current_status: Filed 2026-09-03 while rebuilding the pillar pages. This is the goal that puts Product on fire, and correctly: it is the difference between evidence and a number. Nothing about it is hard — it is a four-field JSON file per session — it has simply never been written down.

plan.step: Agree the four fields and write the schema
Backfill the existing session folders from the roadmap's prose, marked as attested
Teach the session puller to write the record
Have the gate scorecard read it instead of assuming it
